# Installing toolsmith on muse

## What gets emitted

- `.muse-plugin/plugin.json`
- the `hooks/everyharness` bootstrap hook (`session-start` + `run-hook.cmd`)
- the generated bootstrap file at `hooks/everyharness/bootstrap.md`

## Installing

```bash
muse plugins install ./
muse plugins approve superpowers
```

Or clone and install: `git clone https://github.com/owner/repo.git && muse plugins install ./` + `muse plugins approve toolsmith`.

Muse registers the `SessionStart` bootstrap hook — `using-toolsmith` (or the generated bootstrap) is injected automatically every session with no per-session opt-in, alongside the other harnesses. Hooks require approval on first install (`muse plugins approve toolsmith`); skills are active immediately. Restart any active Muse sessions after installing to pick up the hook.

## Caveats

- `muse plugins install` validates the plugin — `muse plugins validate ./` should report `valid` with at most the expected `multiple-manifests` warning when the repo also ships other harness manifests.
- Hooks share the `hooks/everyharness` directory with Claude Code and Cursor so the three adapters coexist; the `session-start` script handles `MUSE_PLUGIN_ROOT` with nested `hookSpecificOutput` (Muse Spark requires nested, not top-level `additionalContext`).
